details:
A way to make your own menu visible to nearby players, for the purpose of walking someone through VRChat's controls.

Problem

Nearly all onboarding in VRChat happens person to person, verbally. But you can't see the other player's screen, so:

"Open your menu, it's the button in the top right" gives you no way to confirm what they're actually looking at

You can't tell whether they're stuck or have wandered into a different submenu

The person explaining can't show what they're pressing

The practical workaround today is pulling up an external video or screenshot. Explaining VRChat's own interface currently requires leaving VRChat.

Proposed shape

When enabled in settings, your menu is mirrored to a panel visible in-world. Cursor position and active tab should be reflected — without those you can't point at anything, which is most of the value.

Handling personal information

Mirroring the real menu would expose friend lists, notifications, profiles, and invite requests. That should not happen. Two options that avoid it:

Demo mode — display a dummy menu containing no real account data. This is sufficient for teaching.

Masked mirror — show the real UI structure but hide friend names, notification contents, and usernames.

Either one supports the actual goal, which is showing where the buttons are and what each screen does. There is no case where real account data needs to be visible.

Settings

Off by default. While active, the sharing player should have a clear indicator that it's on.

Use cases

Official and community tutorial worlds

Group instruction at events (walking a room through a settings change)

One-on-one help for users unfamiliar with the interface
title: Menu sharing / demo mode for teaching new users
